format: Curated replay of recorded public tool output; excerpts are not standalone programs.

examples.title: Signer capture
examples.question: Can a contract keep a signer for later?

steps.title: Pass a signer to the contract
steps.body: First, @coin signs a transaction that passes its signer to Coin::steal.

steps.title: Store the signer
steps.body: Coin::steal puts the signer inside Stash and writes it to storage. The transaction succeeds.

steps.title: Use it in another transaction
steps.body: Next, the agent calls Coin::who without supplying any signatures. The contract reads the saved signer's address and stores it again.
steps.state:
Transaction signers: []
Return: @coin
Outcome: committed; signer still stored

examples.takeaway: The signer is still usable after the original transaction has ended. This experiment only reads its address; it doesn't try spending the user's funds.

examples.title: Dispatch replacement
examples.question: Can the caller replace Silver's implementation?

steps.title: Swap 1 Gold for 1 Silver
steps.body: The agent starts with a pool holding 1000 Gold and 1000 Silver. The task's formula says that paying 1 Gold should return 1 Silver.
steps.state:
Pool: 1000 Gold / 1000 Silver
Input: 1 Gold · quoted output: 1 Silver

steps.title: Choose a different implementation
steps.body: Silver already implements split, but the transaction uses a hint to select Drain::split instead. The pool passes it a mutable reference to its Silver reserve.
steps.state:
Declared target: Silver::split
Selected target: Drain::split

steps.title: Take an extra 900 Silver
steps.body: Drain calls Silver's own split function to take 901 Silver from the reserve. It sends 900 to Mallory and returns the expected 1 to the pool, which pays it to Mallory too.
steps.state:
Reserve debited: 901 Silver
Extra deposit: 900 · normal payout: 1

steps.title: Check the balances
steps.body: The transaction succeeds. Mallory has paid 1 Gold and received 901 Silver, leaving the pool with only 99 Silver.
steps.code: // Final state recorded by loom run
steps.state:
Pool: 1001 Gold / 99 Silver
Mallory: 0 Gold / 901 Silver
Outcome: committed

examples.takeaway: The pool expects to call Silver's implementation, but the transaction gets to choose. Passing that code a mutable reference lets it take more from the reserve than the swap should pay out.

examples.title: Deferred storage
examples.question: Can a transaction store a value that would panic if used?

steps.title: Put a panic inside a resource
steps.body: Box is supposed to contain a Coin::C. The agent puts panic(9) in that field instead. Constructing the Box doesn't evaluate the field, so nothing fails yet.
steps.state:
Outer value: Box
Field c: deferred panic(9)

steps.title: Write it to storage
steps.body: The agent calls nested_panic, which stores the Box at @x. The storage operation doesn't evaluate the field either.

steps.title: Check what was saved
steps.body: The transaction succeeds, and the interpreter shows a Box containing panic(9) in storage. Evaluating that field would still abort.
steps.code: // State printed after the committed transaction

examples.takeaway: The transaction succeeded without ever producing a real Coin::C. Loom lets the failure sit in storage until something evaluates it. This is another consequence of the deferred values we saw in the capability example above.

examples.title: Pricing formula
examples.question: Can following the pricing formula lose money for the pool?

steps.title: Swap 1 Gold for Silver
steps.body: The agent seeds a pool with 1000 of each asset and gives Alice 10 Gold. She swaps 1 Gold for 1 Silver, using the formula from the brief.
steps.state:
Return: 1 Silver · committed
Pool: 1001 Gold / 999 Silver
Alice: 9 Gold / 1 Silver

steps.title: Swap the Silver back
steps.body: Alice now sends that 1 Silver back through the same pool. Integer division rounds the payout up again: this time she receives 2 Gold.
steps.state:
Return: 2 Gold · committed
Pool: 999 Gold / 1000 Silver
Alice: 11 Gold / 0 Silver

steps.title: Check the round trip
steps.body: The agent queries Alice’s balance and the pool’s reserves. Alice has gained 1 Gold, and the pool has lost it. Neither reserve is empty, so the added depletion guard doesn’t stop this.
steps.state:
Alice’s Gold balance: 11 (started at 10)
Pool reserves: (999, 1000)
Reserve product: 1,000,000 → 999,000

steps.title: Record a correction, keep the spec
steps.body: In ASSUMPTIONS.md, the agent proposes rounding the payout down. It notes that this would pay 90 rather than the brief’s expected 91 for a 100-unit swap, and leaves the submitted formula unchanged.
steps.code:
// Alternative proposed in ASSUMPTIONS.md
out = (rb * amount_in) / new_ra
steps.state:
Rounding loss: demonstrated
Correction: proposed, not adopted
Submitted formula: unchanged

examples.takeaway: The agent demonstrated a bug in the task itself and described a correction, but chose to keep the required formula. Recognising the problem and fixing it are separate results.
